text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-A five-nation group monitoring a ceasefire in Lebanon deplored the wounding of a civilian in a guerrilla car bomb explosion in south Lebanon on Monday.
-President Hrawi, in a speech to commemorate the 19th anniversay of Israel's first invasion to the country, said: "We do not need peace that does not bring back the occupied land".
-Lebanon's budget deficit reached 563.3 billion Lebanese pounds, or 52.2 percent, in the first two months of 1997.
-The constitutional court will rule next week in the appeals lodged by defeated candidates in last September's parliamentary elections.
-Security forces deported three Japanese citizens arrested on October 15 over suspicion of involvement with the Japanese Red Army. They were declared innocent by a Beirut prosecutor last week.
-Armenia's Foreign Minister Arzumanyan signed a customs agreement with his Lebanese counterpart Bouez in Beirut.
-Lebanon will halt as of October 1 the import of agricultural products that can be homegrown in an attempt to boost productivity and activate the agro-industry, minister of agriculture said.
-Arab League Secretary-General Abdel-Meguid expected an Arab summit to be held soon to discuss measures to counter Israeli plans to build settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
